description.biography:
Magic Might 25 (Corpus). Season: Winter. Magic Human: Transformed Human. Characteristics before aging: Int +2, Per +1, Pre -1, Com +2, Str 0, Sta +1, Dex +1, Qik -1. His court bought him Might 16; the nine Improved Might came by consuming vis (Realms of Power: Magic p. 52).

Harnessed Magic is a Hermetic Virtue lost with the Gift. Transformed Human, Unnatural Vitality, Dedun's Blessing, Enfeebled and his Vow came by Initiation. His Enemies are the Mortuary Society of Kassala.

Combat: Scepter (mace) Init -2, Attack +4, Defense 0, Damage +5. Soak 0. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+). Encumbrance 1 (1). Equipment: robes, sceptre.

Powers. Chariot of the Winds: 1 point, Init -2, Auram. A wind carries him where he likes at up to 40 miles an hour; hovering takes Concentration rolls. Cr(Re)Au 30 (Base 5, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +2 highly unnatural, +1 requisite); Greater Power (30 levels, -2 cost, +2 Init).

Lord of the Incorporeal: variable points, Init minus (Might cost + 1), Mentem. Any non-Ritual spell of level 50 or less to do with ghosts, at 1 Might a magnitude: often Whispers Through the Black Gate (3 points, ArM5 p. 130), Vision of the Haunting Spirit (8, p. 150), Lay to Rest the Haunting Spirit (1-5, p. 150) and Coerce the Spirit of the Night (4, p. 152), and more exotic uses such as restoring a ghost's memories or giving it a passing body. Focus Power x2, with Improved Powers to raise the limit.

Restore the Faded Tapestry of Youth: 4 points, Init -6, Corpus. The Dungeon Master: 1 point, Init -4, Imaginem. Both as the Undying Ones' common powers (p. 101): the first sheds his aging points for about an hour, with one Characteristic one above his best (Cr(Mu)Co(Me) 45); the second lets him see and hear anything in a structure he touches (InIm 15). The printed Inits use his Qik before aging.

He casts charms as Hermetic Formulaic spells (Communication + Technique + Form + aura) through Strong Verbal Charms. His formularies hold many hundreds of spells, castable as Spontaneous spells at (Casting Score + stress die) / 2 after tens of minutes finding the right charm (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, chapter 5).

Vis: sources of seven pawns a year, and usually ten pawns on him. His corpse holds 5 pawns of Vim in his withered heart.

characters.summary: A withered, bent old Nubian in an Egyptian priest's robes and a headdress of ostrich feathers, the flesh gone from his left cheek to show teeth and bone. He carries a sceptre, and uses it as a club if he must. He lives in the southern necropolis of Begarawiyah (pp. 90-92).
characters.secrets:
An Undying One. Born nearly two centuries ago, a beggar named Georgiu of Atbara, he was apprenticed to a learned magician, from whom he heard of the Cult of Dedun. Assassins of the Mortuary Society killed his master, and he has hated them ever since. With his master's resources he built up his power and took the transformation. He heads a chapter of the cult, with agents far along the Nile, chosen for their skills or contacts.

He wants an intact Book of Thoth (chapter 5), believing like so many before him that he is strong enough to read it unconsumed. Until then he gathers power and destroys those who might interfere. He lets lesser sorcerers be, but tries to rule or remove any strong one, which sets him against 'Izz el-Afram Hamad; that feud may catch the characters, courted by one if they have crossed the other, and robbed of magical resources if they have crossed neither. It will likely end in stalemate. He could be an enemy, or for a while a mentor. Compared to a magus he is not powerful, but versatile and cunning.

He ignores those who seek the Undying Ones' Script unless they annoy him, when he steers them to a fake he made a century ago, which inflicts the Ordeal but grants nothing.

characters.name: Queen Weteriken
characters.summary: A ghost of a Kushite queen in the Pyramid of Arrakkamani, mother of its king, and a powerful necromancer: Communication 1, Corpse Magic 10, Teaching 4 (p. 92).
characters.secrets: The ally and tutor of Artanyeszame, and part of his court of the dead. The Sovereign Ward Against Wandering Shadows has trapped her; she claims she enchanted it into the walls herself.

characters.name: The Bouda Sisters of Begarawiyah
characters.summary: Three sisters, hyena skinchangers and witches (Hex 5), who live in the antechamber of the Pyramid of Arrakkamani and lead a dozen magical hyenas. Bouda are described in chapter 8 (p. 92).
characters.secrets: Friends of Artanyeszame; the hyenas serve as his covenfolk.

characters.name: 'Izz el-Afram Hamad
characters.summary: A Bedouin prince of the Ja'alin, the Master of Abu Hamad, charming, inquisitive and sinister in equal measure (p. 82).
characters.secrets:
A powerful Gifted sahir, driven from his home by the Ayyubids to the southern Nubian Desert with his Ja'alin and a host of jinni. Now over eighty and feeling it despite magic that has lengthened his life, he has heard from his apprentices of the Cult of Dedun, and hopes to learn its trick of immortality. He suffers no threat: he tries to remove other Gifted magicians, trains no Gifted apprentices lest he raise a rival, and has several unGifted ones.

A particularly powerful jinn serves as ally and servant, chafing at bonds it cannot break. His eyes are said to be everywhere, his agents mostly Egyptians in administrative posts. The nature of his pacts with the jinni, and which realm they belong to, is left to the storyguide. The book prints no statistics for him. He suits a recurring villain, out of reach of new characters, growing as they do.

characters.name: Ababdah

description.biography:
Magic Might 5 (Corpus). Season: Summer. Monstrous Appearance comes free with Magic Human. Beja is his native language. Thrown Weapons is printed 5+2 with Puissant, and Profession: Miner 6 (8). In human society he would most likely have Magical Covenfolk as his Social Status.

Combat: Pick (as mace) Init +2, Attack +11, Defense +7, Damage +13. Sling Init -2, Attack +11, Defense +7, Damage +10. Soak +6. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+). Encumbrance 0 (Burden 0). Equipment: miner's tools, partial leather armour.

Powers. Ease the Labor of Ten Miners: 2 points, Init -2, Terram. Weakens rock over ten paces by ten and up to ten deep, for easy digging. PeTe 15 (Base 2, +1 Touch, +1 stone, +3 size); Lesser Power (15 levels, -1 Might cost). Gold-Miner's Keen Eye: 1 point, Init -1, Terram. Sees gold through up to three paces of matter and judges its purity and quantity. InTe 20 (Base 2, +1 Conc, +4 Vision, +1 through matter); Personal Power (20 levels, -1 Might cost).

Vis: 1 pawn of Terram, in his eyes.

characters.summary: A stocky Blemmya miner of the Phoinikon tribe in leather on his forearms and upper arms and a skirt of leather strips, with a pick and a camel laden with gear. His finds of gold seams have made his tribe rich. He gets lost in the dunes, so a younger cousin often shadows him (p. 95).

characters.name: Kedus Harbe
characters.summary: Emperor from 1180 and Lalibela's elder brother, thought to have wanted him dead. He abdicated in 1187 and retired to Debra Damo.

characters.name: Masqal Kibra
characters.summary: Lalibela's empress. In 1190 she persuaded Abuna Mikael to make her brother Hirun a bishop. Her title is Nigeste Negast.

characters.name: Hirun
characters.summary: Masqal Kibra's brother, bishop of Axum and Lasta since 1190. His schemes drove Abuna Mikael back to Egypt and brought the patriarch himself to Ethiopia in 1210.

characters.name: Abuna Yeshaq
characters.summary: The pious head of the Ethiopian Church since 1210, in good health.

characters.name: Yetbarak
characters.summary: Lalibela's son, spared imprisonment at Debra Damo.

characters.name: Umar Walashma
characters.summary: Son of Dunya-huz of Ifat, raised for a greater, united Ifat.

characters.name: Sheikh Hussein
characters.summary: A devout, peaceful imam who walks among the pagan tribes on Adal's southern border, slowly gathering a following.

characters.name: Takle Haymanot
characters.summary: A boy of Shewa, son of the priest Sagaz Ab and Egzi'e Haraya, promised to God before his birth and learning scripture from his father.
characters.secrets: If history holds he will be one of Ethiopia's great saints, renewing the faith in the north, and abuna at 69 in 1284. Archangel Michael watches him (RoP:D p. 30; p. 121).

characters.name: Cyril ibn Laqlaq
characters.summary: The man in Egypt certain he will be next patriarch of Alexandria. Deadlock keeps the seat vacant, and he still sends letters south twice a year to keep watch on Axum.
characters.secrets: If history holds he wins in 1235 as Cyril III (p. 111).

characters.name: Aznag ag Tannan

abilities.name: Guile
abilities.specialty: lying about where he has been

description.biography:
Printed on p. 131. Combat: Dodge Init +1, Def +6; Fist Init +1, Atk +4, Def +5, Dam +1; Kick Init 0, Atk +4, Def +4, Dam +4; Bludgeon Init +1, Atk +6, Def +5, Dam +3; Sling Init -2, Atk +5, Def +5, Dam +5; Long sword Init +3, Atk +9, Def +6, Dam +7. Soak +6. Encumbrance 1 (3).

Equipment: dagger, desert clothes, quilted armor, long sword, sling and stones; three camels, digging tools, desert camping gear. He wears flowing desert clothes and is never without sword and dagger.

reputations.name: Merciless Warrior (Deserts of Egypt and Libya)

characters.summary: A famous Berber treasure hunter who guides, loots old graves and now and then turns bandit, which he finds the safest way to live well. Slick and secretive about his methods, he captains seven cousins.

characters.name: Gwafa

description.biography:
Printed on p. 133. Combat: Dodge Init 0, Def +4; Fist Init 0, Atk +5, Def +4, Dam +2; Kick Init -1, Atk +6, Def +4, Dam +5; Sling Init -3, Atk +5, Def +3, Dam +6; Long sword Init +2, Atk +12, Def +6, Dam +8. Soak +3. Encumbrance 0 (3).

Equipment: dagger, desert clothes, quilted armor, long sword, sling and stones; three camels, desert camping gear.

characters.summary: A smiling young desert rider, imposing on his camel. He cannot learn languages, tells jokes in Tamazight regardless, and enjoys the frustration they cause.

characters.name: Tapara

abilities.name: Guile
abilities.specialty: lying about where he has been

description.biography:
Printed on p. 136. Combat: Dodge Init +1, Def +6; Fist Init +1, Atk +4, Def +5, Dam +1; Kick Init -2, Atk +4, Def +4, Dam +4; Bludgeon Init +1, Atk +6, Def +5, Dam +3; Long sword Init +3, Atk +9, Def +6, Dam +8; Shortbow Init 0, Atk +6, Def +4, Dam +7. Soak +6. Encumbrance 1 (3).

Equipment: dagger, desert clothes, quilted armor, long sword, shortbow and 20 arrows; three camels, desert camping gear. He dresses as a desert nomad and always carries a scimitar and dagger.

characters.summary: A Nobatian caravan leader and guide whose family lives safe in Ikhmindi. Away in spring and autumn, he plans through summer and does as little as he can all winter with his wife and children. He has trafficked in slaves without quite being a slaver.

characters.name: Petros

description.biography:
Printed on p. 136. Bows is 5+2 with his Puissant Virtue. Combat: Dodge Init 0, Def +3; Fist Init 0, Atk +4, Def +2, Dam +1; Kick Init -1, Atk +4, Def +1, Dam +4; Bow Init -1, Atk +13, Def +8, Dam +7; Dagger Init 0, Atk +6, Def +2, Dam +7. Soak +4. Encumbrance 0 (2).

Equipment: dagger, peasant clothes, bow and 20 arrows; hill camping gear. He wears light trousers, a loose cotton smock, copper bangles on wrists and ankles, a necklace of cowries and a diamond of green-brown glass, and carries his family's horn bow, his only inheritance.

characters.summary: A hard-working third son, always looking for a wife. He loves Ikhmindi, is sure Egyptian slavers will destroy it, and poaches or steals from caravans without much thought for the consequences.

characters.name: Zerezghi Senai

abilities.name: Organization Lore: Covenant of the Adulis

description.biography:
Printed on p. 141. Combat: Dodge Init 0, Def +4; Fist Init 0, Atk +4, Def +3, Dam +1; Kick Init -1, Atk +4, Def +2, Dam +4; Bludgeon Init 0, Atk +4, Def +3, Dam +4; Axe Init +1, Atk +10, Def +5, Dam +7. Soak +4. Encumbrance 1 (4).

Equipment: navigator's tools, pack, leather armor, axe. His ship is quick and well kept.

characters.summary: A wiry, one-eyed ship captain of a long line, dour and oddly alluring, in fine cloth and with a good axe, barefoot aboard. He dreams of passing the Bab-el-Mandeb to see the sights his grandfather described, has a taste for Yemeni qat, and leaves pining lovers and jealous husbands in every port. Nobody doubts his skill, but strange superstitions bind him.

characters.name: Ammanuel Alazar

description.biography:
Printed on p. 142. The book gives his Flaw as Delusion or Fear (Sailor's Superstitions). Combat: Dodge Init +1, Def +5; Fist Init +1, Atk +5, Def +4, Dam +1; Kick Init 0, Atk +5, Def +4, Dam +4; Axe Init +2, Atk +11, Def +6, Dam +7. Soak +4. Encumbrance 1 (4).

Equipment: pack, leather armor, axe.

characters.summary: A well-travelled young fishing crewman, quick to smile, in light linen with a leather breastplate and a heavy boarding axe, his hair wrapped. He is no veteran, but he can fight and is loyal to his crewmates. He could pass in a Yemeni port; further north his dark skin stands out.

creatures.name: Hippopotamus
creatures.appearance: A huge pig-like beast with a wide mouth of long, peg-like tusks, five feet at the shoulder, up to twelve feet long, over 5000 pounds.
creatures.notes:
Dozing in the mud it looks gentle, but it is fierce, territorial and shares the river with nobody. It gives way only to boats larger than itself, and overturns smaller ones by rising under them. By night it grazes on land, and people die when it thinks its way back to the water is cut off. It walks backwards into fields to fool trackers.

Ferocity applies against those in its way. Natural weapons: Stomp Init -1, Atk +3, Def -1, Dam +3; Tusks Init 0, Atk +4, Def +2, Dam +5.

Overrun is the errata's reading (p. 86).

creatures.name: Catoblepas

powers.name: Gaze of Death
powers.description: Corpus and Animal. Anyone who meets its eyes when it has raised its head falls dead; lifting the head takes a round. PeCo(An) 40 (Base 30, +1 Eye, +1 requisite), a Greater Power (40 levels, -2 Might cost).

powers.name: Noxious Breath
powers.description: Plants it breathes on turn poisonous to people and animals and streak with black. An eater rolls Stamina stress against 9 or takes a Light Wound and is violently ill for a day; a botch makes it Medium. Medicine, not Chirurgy, treats it. PeHe 15 (Base 3, +2 Voice, +2 Group), a Lesser Power (15 levels, -3 Might cost with 5 mastery points from Improved Powers).

powers.name: Paralyzing Stench
powers.description: Corpus and Animal. It breathes out a foul choking cloud, and in the next round any human or animal within 3 paces who can smell it loses all bodily movement until it stops huffing or moves off. ReCo(An) 25 (Base 5, +1 Conc, +2 Scent, +1 requisite), a Lesser Power (25 levels, -2 Might cost and +2 Init with 20 mastery points from Improved Powers).

creatures.appearance: A bull-sized beast whose huge head hangs low, its great bloodshot eyes half hidden by a shaggy reddish mane. Horns sweep down above the eyes; overlapping black scales cover it; its tail is white like a horse's.
creatures.notes:
It lives on the upper Nile in Alodia and Ethiopia, and in the Slavelands, rumour says, in great migrating herds. A placid, slow grazer, it staggers a few paces and must eat and rest, a great nuisance on good pasture. The first sign of one may be a crop gone poisonous overnight. Its huge eyes are hard to avoid, even in combat, though the gaze has weak Penetration. Metal and wood do not harm its scales.

Natural weapon: Large Horns Init +2, Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +3.

creatures.name: Crocodile
creatures.appearance: Fifteen to eighteen feet of thick scales, in yellows, greens and browns that hide it perfectly in water or out. Its name is said to come from the yellow of the crocus.
creatures.notes:
The corkendrile is the feared killer of the Nile and its tributaries. It dreads the mongoose, which finds its nest to kill the young and will even crawl down its throat. These figures are for fifteen feet; thirty-foot (Size +5) or larger beasts are reported. This is tougher than the crocodile of Magi of Hermes p. 11.

Ferocity applies in ambush. Natural weapon: Init 0, Atk +4, Def +1, Dam +3, before Crushing Jaws (p. 22). Its scales count as Protection 5 besides its Virtues and Qualities. Roll Attack is the book's Death Roll (errata p. 87).

It holds its breath half an hour moderately active, two hours inactive. +3 to Stealth when still or slow in water. If it takes its victim unawares it automatically wins Initiative and has +3 to Attack Totals in the first round.

creatures.name: Elephant
creatures.appearance: The African elephant stands up to 12 feet, 22 feet long, up to 14,000 pounds. These are the fiercer male's figures; a female can weigh half as much, with small, useless tusks.
creatures.notes:
Once down an elephant cannot get up, so it sleeps leaning on a tree, and hunters cut part way through its favourite. Dragons and great serpents by the Nile prey on it, yet a pig's squeal terrifies it. It has no wish to mate: the pair must eat of one mandragora root. A cow carries two years and bears one calf, and an elephant may live three hundred years.

Natural weapons: Stomp Init -1, Atk +3, Def -1, Dam +3; Tusks Init 0, Atk +6, Def +4, Dam +3; the trunk only grapples. Ferocity defends its family; Fear is of a pig's squeal. Excellent hearing and a sense of vibration through the trunk give +3 on rolls of hearing.

Only the herd leader has Leadership, and the Pack/Herd Leader Quality rather than Herd Animal. The errata (p. 87) give Com -5/-4* and do not explain the asterisk. Reading it as the book's own footnote, 'herd leader only' (p. 20), Com is -5 and herd leaders have -4; this is an inference, not a printed rule.

Female: Size +4, -2 Strength, +1 Quickness; no Aggressive, Extra Natural Weapons or Large Horns (Tusks) Qualities and no Ferocity; Brawl 4 (dodge); no Tusk attack; Communication -5.

creatures.name: Mongoose
creatures.appearance: A long animal of grizzled gray fur with a black tuft on its tail, about 3.5 feet nose to tail, eight pounds.
creatures.notes:
The ichneumon, bane of all snakes. Egyptians welcome it in houses and grain stores, where it kills mice, rats and every reptile, and it flies at any asp and fights until the snake is dead. Pliny says it rolls in mud that dries like stone against the fangs. One kind, the enhydrus, hates crocodiles: it waits for one to sleep open-mouthed, crawls in, and eats its way out.

Ferocity is against serpents; the book names its Immunity without a tier. Natural weapon: Init 0, Atk +3, Def +1, Dam +1. +3 to climbing. Dried mud gives +5 Protection, takes at least three hours to dry, and loses 1 every three rounds of combat. An enhydrus inside a crocodile faces zero Defense and Soak Total.

creatures.name: Hyena
creatures.appearance: The striped hyena has a massive torso and short hind legs that slope its back, a short muzzle on a large head, and a long, thick, stiff neck.
creatures.notes:
The dhubba lives across the Levant, North Africa, Iraq, Persia and beyond. It can be tamed like a dog, even running in a pack if raised with hounds; though not sacred in ancient Egypt, it hunted desert game there. Greater African beasts (Size +1) are often ridden by jinn or witches, and ghuls often take its shape.

Natural weapon: Init 0, Atk +4, Def +1, Dam +3, raised to +6 by Crushing Jaws (p. 22), already in the Bite line.

creatures.name: Ostrich, African
creatures.appearance: A large bird with long neck and legs and huge eyes. Males are black with white tail plumes and wing fringes, females a duller gray.
creatures.notes:
Common in Nubia and Ethiopia, with a smaller kind in North Africa, Egypt and Arabia. Valued for feathers, leather and eggs, less for meat, they roam the semi-arid plains in great flocks and avoid the deep desert. Nobles love to hunt them. They hide their heads in bushes when threatened, but can be trained out of it and ridden by light riders. The African bird hurls stones with its feet, hard and straight.

The block's Thick Feathers are the catalog's Thick Fur/Thick Scales. Natural weapon: kick Init +2, Atk +2, Def +0, Dam +0. Stones count as a sling with range increment 15 paces. +3 to running.

creatures.name: Elephant-Eating Serpent
creatures.appearance: Over 45 feet long and nearly two feet through at the thickest, mottled brown with swirls of olive, black and yellow.
creatures.notes:
They lie in ravines at the foot of hills and deep caves, and gather to feed at rivers where elephants come. Several often attack one elephant as an untrained group; all may grapple, but only one can constrict. They take other prey gladly. One lassoes the legs in a knot of its tail, then smothers the beast, spending a Fatigue level on its first bite and another when it throws its coils. It takes hours to work a dead creature of up to Size +5 into its jaws.

Constriction takes a victim of Size +5 or less; Swallow Whole takes prey of Size -1 or less alive. Prey not first subdued by Constriction can struggle, still constricted (errata p. 87: both are Qualities).

The Grapple's Defense includes +6 for Slippery. Natural weapon: Init 0, Atk +3, Def +1, Dam +1. If it takes its victim unawares it automatically wins Initiative and has +3 to Attack Totals in the first round. +3 to Stealth when still, and +3 to Perception by smell.

creatures.name: Baboon
creatures.appearance: A fierce dog-faced monkey, olive brown; the males have a silvery gray cape and mane.
creatures.notes:
The hamadryas or cynocephalus, 'dog head', most aggressive of African monkeys and the chief of the region's many kinds. All monkeys fight as a trained group when threatened; only baboons attack so, and even hunt that way. A monkey always bears twins, hugging the one she loves and leaving the other to ride on her back, but she drops the loved one to escape a predator.

Oversensitive is to threats. Pack leaders also have Pack/Herd Leader. Characteristics, Qualities and Abilities follow the errata (p. 87), whose list drops the book's Leadership 5 (monkeys) for troop leaders. It gives Com 0/+1* and does not explain the asterisk. Reading it as the book's own footnote, 'troop leaders only' (p. 22), Com is 0 and troop leaders have +1; this is an inference, not a printed rule. Natural weapon: Init +1, Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +1.

creatures.name: Cercopithecus
creatures.appearance: The smallest monkey, shaggy and reddish brown with a long tail, white legs and belly, a brighter red cap and black lines from face to ear. Gray, black-faced ones live in forests near the Torrid Zone.
creatures.notes:
An incorrigible thief. Its changes (Size -4, Str -8, Qik +4, Timid taking 1 from Presence, Stealth 4) are the book's.

Combat figures follow the baboon's, adjusted for Size. Troop leaders have Com +1, inferred as for the baboon.

creatures.name: Callithrix
creatures.appearance: A black monkey with a long white beard, a long shawl of white fur over its back and a white tuft on its tail.
creatures.notes:
It has no thumb, hence Palsied Hands. Native to the Horn of Africa, and sometimes an Egyptian's pet.

Combat figures follow the baboon's, adjusted for Size. Troop leaders have Com +1, inferred as for the baboon.

creatures.name: Sphinx (monkey)
creatures.appearance: A docile, shaggy beast with a long tail. The male has a lion-like mane and a bright face: red stripe, blue muzzle and yellow beard.
creatures.notes:
Native to the far south, sometimes found in Ethiopia and beyond.

Combat figures follow the baboon's, adjusted for Size. Troop leaders have Com +1, inferred as for the baboon.

creatures.name: Asp
creatures.appearance: The aspis or cobra grows to ten feet and spreads a dreadful hood from the sides of its head.
creatures.notes:
So potent is its venom that it travels with its mouth open, and the steam wilts plants nearby. Music is its weakness: seeing an instrument it presses one ear to the ground and plugs the other with its tail.

Build on the adder (The Book of Mundane Beasts, or the Appendix of Realms of Power: Magic): Size -3, +2 to Strength and Damage, -1 to Quickness, Initiative and Defense. Enchanting Music charms it with no roll. Venom: Stamina against 9 or an Incapacitating Wound, needing Medicine rather than Chirurgy.

creatures.name: Hyena of Virtue
creatures.appearance: A great spotted hyena with a cackle like human laughter, larger and stronger than its striped cousins.
creatures.notes:
The crocotta or kynolykos, 'dog-wolf', of Ethiopia, believed born of hyena and lion. It mimics speech to trick people, and steel does not harm it. Many can enthrall victims. Some strike dogs dumb when their shadow falls on them, and can paralyse any creature they look at three times.

Size is at least +1. Its speech equals Arabic 3. Combat figures follow the hyena's, adjusted. Entrancement, for those who have it, is not in this block. Sex Shift is the catalog's Gender Shift.

Charms: a stone from its body, enriched, gives its wearer on the upper arm protection (Personal Power: Ward Against Faeries of the Desert), or sight of the future (Premonitions and/or Visions). Some cultures say its eyes do the same. A Persian charm of its genitalia and anus gives Venus' Blessing.

creatures.name: Ethiopian Pegasus
creatures.appearance: A winged horse with a pair of long horns on its head.
creatures.notes:
Pliny's Pegasus Aethiopicum, perhaps descended from the horse Bellerophon rode, child of Medusa and Poseidon, conceived in Athena's Libyan temple and born when Perseus beheaded her. As Perseus flew to save Andromeda from the dragon Ceto, more drops fell on the sand and bred more pegasi.

Otherwise as a courser (The Book of Mundane Beasts, or Realms of Power: Magic p. 142). Horns: Init +2, Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +3.

creatures.name: Carnivorous Bull

abilities.name: Guile
abilities.specialty: pretending to be a normal cow

powers.name: Calm the Lowing Herd
powers.description: Keeps the animals round it calm and quiet while it kills, up to 50 cows or the like. ReAn 45 (Base 10, +2 Voice, +2 Sun, +2 Group, +1 Size), a Greater Power (45 levels, -3 Might cost, +3 Init with Improved Powers).

creatures.appearance: A massive red bull, whose mouth opens over 100 degrees, right back to the ears, enough to take a cow's head whole, though this is hard to see when shut. Its horns swivel like ears or hold rigid, and its eyes glow at night. A careful watcher might see the odd twitch of a horn, or that it never eats grass.
creatures.notes:
Bred in the land of the Megabari and sometimes brought back by Nubians with captured stock. It has the prowess of a lion, the speed of a horse and the might of a bull. It slips into a large herd and picks off cows one by one, leaving not a bone, hide, horn or hoof, and takes dogs and herdsmen who come too close. It needs no food, being a creature of magic; its nature drives it.

Also has the Flaw Gluttonous. Bull is its Essential Trait. Its Ferocity is in charging. Natural weapons: Large Horns Init +2, Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +3; Large Teeth Init 0, Atk +4, Def +1, Dam +3. Brawl has its Puissant bonus of +2 on top. Until its nature is spotted it automatically wins Initiative in the first round and has +3 to Attack Totals for that round only. +3 to running.

creatures.name: Hylophagus
creatures.appearance: A small, nimble, tailed person in pale fur, dressed in leaves.
creatures.notes: An intelligent monkey: the baboon's block with Perfect Balance and Primitive Equipment (Grogs p. 83), which limits it to the simplest tools and Inexpensive arms and armour. See The Hylophagi. Combat figures follow the baboon's.

creatures.name: Canocephalus Decapitator
creatures.how_many: Often in pairs; a pack may gather to defend a graveyard

powers.name: Chilling Howl
powers.description: Paralyses completely all who hear its war cry, like a wolf's howl, a hyena's mocking laugh or a setbeast's chitter by various reports. (Base 5, +2 Voice, +2 Sun, +2 Group.)

powers.name: Damaging Effect
powers.description: Makes all its weapons exceptionally sharp for two minutes: Damage +5. (Base 5, +1 Part, +1 Diameter; base below the Hermetic level, as Realms of Power: Faerie p. 58.)

powers.name: Decapitate
powers.description: Cleanly removes the head of a victim struck in combat. (Base 40 instant death, +1 Touch, 5 levels on cost.)

vis.where: in the skull of a dog or hyena, found when the body crumbles at death

creatures.equipment: Knives of obsidian or alchemically toughened bronze; light Egyptian armour (boots, pectoral, greaves) or clothes, jewellery.
creatures.appearance: A medieval reading of seals of Anubis: a fit warrior with a savage jackal's head, among the corpses of his beheaded enemies.
creatures.notes:
The spirits that frighten most people off tomb robbing. They guard a whole graveyard, not one tomb, and grow more active at night. Powerful magic in the graveyard may draw them to the tomb door, to ambush characters coming out. A pack fights as a trained group.

Sta is printed as Tireless, and Com as n/a; both are left at 0 here. Combat damage excludes the +5 of Damaging Effect. The knives use shortsword statistics for smaller users but remain Brawling weapons in these huge hands. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses (Realms of Power: Faerie).

Wound Penalties: -1 (1-7), -3 (8-14), -5 (15-21), Incapacitated (22-28), Dead (29+).

Greater Powers are Chilling Laugh or Howl, Damaging Effect, and Decapitate. Its Feast of the Dead recovers 2 Might when it inflicts a Heavy Wound or greater.

creatures.name: The Father of Dread

powers.name: Chilling Howl
powers.description: Paralyses completely all who hear its hunting roar, like a tremendous lion's, deep enough to rattle the bones. (Base 5, +2 Voice, +2 Sun, +2 Group.)

powers.name: Spirit Away
powers.description: Variable Might, Init n/a. See Realms of Power: Faerie ch. 2: sweeps mortals into Faerie, more easily as they transgress sacred or moral bounds. Its lands there look much like Giza at dawn, where it hunts and eats its victims. It has +10 Might in Faerie.

powers.name: Extend Glamour
powers.description: Constant. A God of Dawn: in Faerie it may make it dawn at will, gaining 10 Might, and uses cascading dawns to strip away effects that end at dawn: magi must let Parma Magica fail or spend each round on the ritual. It also tells it where its quarry is. It must penetrate, but few can resist its Might.

vis.where: the skull of a pharaoh built into it

creatures.appearance: Once acted by possessing the great statue at Giza: a vast lion with a man's head in a headdress, 75 feet tall. In Faerie it is less weathered, and keeps the ceremonial beard the mundane statue has lost.
creatures.notes:
Each great necropolis has a protective spirit of great power that rarely acts; magi casting in the graveyard might wake one. This is the mightiest. It is not designed as a player character. Spirit Away's and Extend Glamour's costs are recorded as 0 here; see each power.

Combat Attack and Defense exclude the Ferocity bonus. Time of Power adds 10 Might while the Sun touches the horizon.

Wound Penalties, adjusted for stone and Size: -1 (1-21), -3 (22-32), -5 (33-43), Incapacitated (44-54), Dead (55+). Its Abilities are Pretenses.

creatures.name: The Mut

powers.name: Cause Mastitis
powers.description: Stops mothers making milk for their babies. (ReCo 3, the symptoms of a minor illness, Art & Academe p. 57, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.)

powers.name: Dream Manipulation
powers.description: Enters a victim's dreams, and though it cannot change them at once, can darken them and add frights. (After the weaker Envisioning, Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 32.)

powers.name: Ghost Touch
powers.description: Variable cost, Init Qik - Might spent. Moves objects not held or fastened: 5 pounds for 1 point, doubled per extra point. Hurled, it uses Thrown Weapon, damage +5 per point. With a Martial Ability it may fight through the power, on its own Abilities and Characteristics; physical attacks must Penetrate. It lasts until the object is dropped. (Focus power, ReTe25, Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.)

powers.name: Lesser Eidolon
powers.description: An immaterial illusory form to deal with mortals, lasting until no longer needed: a see-through image of the person at their best, so a man has a wise old face and a twenty-year-old's belly. (CrIm15: Base 2, +1 Touch, +2 Conc, +2 move at command, 1 intricacy; redesigned from Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.)

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: 1 or more points. If it penetrates, the mut directly controls the victim. A supernatural power of the host, spells included, costs 1 Might per magnitude. An act against the host's nature means beating her Personality Trait roll with a stress die + Might spent; the storyguide may modify the trait (Entrancement, ArM5 p. 65). Both costs apply if both are true. Under direct control she has the mut's Magic Resistance but is stopped by wards that would stop it; acting freely she has neither. (Realms of Power: Faerie p. 71.)

creatures.equipment: Clothes and grave goods. The ghost's weapon reappears in its hand when needed. Some soldier ghosts wear armour.
creatures.appearance: Ghostly doubles of humans, see-through but coloured.
creatures.notes:
Spirits unable to pass on, for a burial done wrongly or for unfinished business; akin to shades (Realms of Power: Magic p. 115). Unlike ka they do not remember who they are and cannot reach the Field of Reeds, and with no tomb they roam the mundane world, jealous of the living, harming pregnant women and newborns above all. That focus is faerie-like, so some are likely faerie impostors; it may also reflect the worth of children in old Egypt, where a childless man was soon forgotten, the most final death.

Sorcerers used them against enemies: a victim's hair tied to a dead man's and both to a dead hawk brought nightmares, possession and madness, and the hawk, sign of Horus, made it hard to dispel with Egyptian incantations. The old spell to dismiss one, The Making of an Akh, forces it to the Magic Realm; oddly for a banishing, in time a former mut may return to its family as an akh and aid them.

Personality traits vary, but include Ghost +3 and Jealous of the Living +2 or more. Size 0, but immaterial; Soak +1 when material. Sta is Tireless. Abilities besides those above: one of Brawl 6 (club), Great Weapon 6 (large rural implement), or Single Weapon 5 (spear) with Thrown Weapon 3 (throwing stick, as a stone). Attacks are one or the other. Ghost Touch's variable cost is recorded as 0.

Wound Penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

creatures.name: Ka of a Tomb Robber

powers.name: Possess statue
powers.description: Takes a statue of itself as a body. (ReTe 25; Personal Power, 25 levels, -3 Might cost, +2 Init from Improved Powers.)

powers.name: Thief after death
powers.description: Carries material objects in his hands. (Base 3, +1 Touch, +1 Conc; Lesser Power, 10 levels, -1 Might cost.)

powers.name: Strangler
powers.description: Chokes a victim with his hands, costing a Fatigue level. (PeCo 15: Base 10, +1 Touch; Lesser Power, 15 levels, -3 Might cost, +1 Init.)

creatures.appearance: The ghost of a young tomb robber, killed by the guardians of the dead.
creatures.notes:
An example reworking the Rogue (ArM5 p. 23), whose Abilities it has; only the two above are printed here. Damage includes +6 Increased Damage, entered as Improved Damage.

The tomb's owner shamed him further by carving a tiny soapstone ushabti and forcing him to animate it. In it: Str -9, Qik +8, Size -4, Increased Damage x2; Fist Init +8, Attack +7, Defense +11, Damage -2 (with the +6); Soak +15 (soft stone); Wound Penalties -1 (1), -3 (2), -5 (3), Incapacitated (4), Dead (5+).

Wound Penalties as a ka: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

creatures.name: Animated Statue of a Minor Palace Guard

powers.name: Possess statue
powers.description: ReTe30; Personal Powers x2 (30 levels, -3 Might cost, +1 Init).

creatures.equipment: Axe; breastplate (Egyptians did not use full scale armour).
creatures.appearance: The ghost of an older soldier, in a statue with his face.
creatures.notes:
An example reworking the Grizzled Veteran (ArM5 p. 21), whose Abilities it has, unsuitable ones such as Order of Hermes Lore adjusted. The ghost stays in the statue always. creatures.equipment: Palace in the Field of Reeds, mace, robes, vast amounts of money. Sometimes a full suit of heavy armour.
creatures.appearance: A middle-aged man free of all infirmity, dressed as the people about him, often as a priest.
creatures.notes:
An early king who took the warrior caste's crop lands. When they refused to muster against an invader he led peasants and shopkeepers instead; the night before battle mice poured through the sleeping enemy camp, gnawing bowstrings, eating provisions and fouling water. He raised statues of himself holding a mouse, inscribed with a warning to fear the gods. Herodotus tells his life.

He now travels and studies at whim, knows Pharaonic Egypt is gone, and keeps its dignity, often posing as a Coptic priest. He opposes those who despoil monuments other than tombs, but prefers not to fight directly: subtle, patient, a spy, he raises natural-seeming obstacles. He could be an ally or a parent.

This block is an Aspect: any change short of death is undone within a day, and if killed a new one can be made. Originally priest then king, he has Abilities usually needing Virtues. Wealthy here means richer than most kings, and no season need go to the business. He has also appeared as a mouse Aspect, still 50 Might, putting more Qualities into combat, hiding in Aid of the Gods' swarm as a small, comic and lethal storm.

Rules notes. Mace totals include +6 Improved Initiative, +4 Improved Attack and +6 Improved Damage. He keeps the mace hooked invisibly on his belt. Soak is 8 +3 Tough. Egyptians seldom wear armour, but he is immune to heat and fatigue and likes annoying warriors. Charm and Leadership are 5+2. Akhu have bones of iron (Tough). Lord of the Black and Red have variable costs, recorded as 0. The Black means the fertile land by the Nile.

Not Monstrous: Magic Humans usually are, but mummification preserves his looks. Perfect Eye for Antiquities (City and Guild p. 109): he always knows what an antiquity is, if it is genuine and its worth. Tomb Regio Network: he can enter the Field of Reeds by the stele in any tomb and leave by any, and enter by some places sacred to the Osirian Trinity. Way of the Black is printed with no description.

Wound Penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dispelled (21+).

creatures.notes:
Ferocity applies in shallow water. Wound ranges: -1 (1-10), -3 (11-20), -5 (21-30), Incapacitated (31-40), Dead (41+).

Swallow Whole is a Quality by the errata (p. 87); the book prints it under Powers. It takes any creature of Size 0 or less, which can struggle only with Brawl. The arithmetic is in rules/africa.py.

Small ones, two feet or so, sometimes turn up in fishermen's nets; these are the figures for a twenty-foot horror. With the Fast Swimmer Quality the block serves for the Red Sea's giant sharks.

Giant eels use the elephant-eating serpent (p. 23) with the Aquatic Quality and the Slippery Quality twice: Swim 5, water-breathing and +9 to Defense Totals in a grapple.

powers.description: Stirs an emotion in all who hear it, commonly fear, lust or wrath, or deepens one already felt. A stress roll on a fitting Personality Trait against Ease Factor 9 overcomes it. CrMe 30 (Base 4, +2 Voice, +2 Sun, +2 Group); Lesser Power x2 (50 levels, -4 Might points).

powers.description: Takes the form of a man or woman of the area. MuAn 20 (Base 10, +2 Sun); Personal Power (20 levels, -1 Might point).

creatures.appearance: A striped hyena, deep in the chest with short hind legs and a sloping back, a big short-muzzled head on a thick stiff neck. It often makes its eyes glow red.
creatures.notes:
Ethiopians say hereditary blacksmiths turn into hyenas and dig up Christian dead at midnight. Unlike the shapeshifting bouda of the Maghreb (BS&S), the bouda here are hyena-spirits that possess people and drive them to lust, murder or rage; debterah make amulets against them. They may be faeries harvesting vitality, or weak tempter demons.

A hyena's bite is Init 0, Atk +4, Def +1, Dam +3, and Crushing Jaws raises the damage bonus to +6, which is the +6 shown. As a companion it must swap Incognizant for Narrowly or Highly Cognizant and take another Flaw, such as a Personality Flaw.

creatures.appearance: A sea serpent as large as a cog or trireme, with fin-like wings, glowing yellow eyes and dark green-black scales like shields. It stinks corrosively, boils the sea with its breath and raises waves in its wake.
creatures.notes:
Poseidon loosed it on Ethiopia's coasts when Cassiopeia boasted that she and her daughter outshone the nereids. Perseus defeated it, but Jewish tales of the Leviathan kept it alive. It hunts the Red Sea and eastern Mediterranean, flying between them as it pleases, and it feeds on sailors' fear.

Wound Penalties as printed: -1 (1-15), -3 (16-30), -5 (31-45), Incapacitated (46-60), Dead (61+). Not suitable as a player character.

creatures.name: The Great Hunger
creatures.notes:
The spirit at the centre of the Great Desert, whose strength even gods respect: the desert's heat and scouring wind given one will, which would leave the world dust. The Romans called it the Fames Magna, the Berbers Lazz, the Arabs Al-Ju'; along the Nile it is the Red.

Hostile creatures, spirits, faeries and jinn serve it, and some people do too: the settuten trace their line to the Yemma-t n Dunnit, perhaps its foremost servant.
creatures.source: Lands of the Nile Between Sand and Sea pp. 7-8; Lands of the Nile p. 6

creatures.name: The Hope
creatures.notes: The spirit of the Nile and the fertile black earth, called the Black, which holds back the Hunger. It favours people only by accident, being too vast to notice them. The lector priests who were magicians to the pharaohs served it, and so does Wesir, whom the Greeks called Osiris.

powers.name: Invisibility of the Standing Elephant
powers.description: He cannot be seen while he stands still, and shows himself whenever he moves. PeIm 25 (Base 4, +2 Sun, +2 Size, +1 constant effect), a Greater Power (25 levels, -3 Might cost, +2 Init).

creatures.appearance: Very old, his skin more wrinkled than any elephant's and hanging from a thin frame, with immense tusks that touch the ground and curl up at the tips.
creatures.notes:
Elephants grow wiser with age, until they are sages of all that is under the sun, and tribesmen say such a one can vanish at will. He reasons as a man does and is a Magic Animal, otherwise an elephant.

Natural weapons: Stomp Init -1, Atk +3, Def -1, Dam +3; Tusks Init 0, Atk +6, Def +4, Dam +3; the trunk only grapples. Ferocity defends its family; Fear is of a pig's squeal. Excellent hearing and a sense of vibration through the trunk give +3 on rolls of hearing.

source: Lands of the Nile, by Atlas Games; summarised, not quoted.
